_readme: Names each OpenAlex cohort export and states what it measures, so a percentile
can never be computed against a cohort that measures a different field.
The CSVs carry no topic column and no identifier -- columns are Title, Author,
Year, Citation count, Open access and optionally FWCI -- so the FILE is the
cohort and files must never be concatenated. One OQL query, one file, one entry.
field:  'glyco' or 'anti'  -> ranks only papers of that programme (and 'both' papers)
'broad'             -> keyword cohort spanning both; ranks any paper but is
labelled broad and is never the exact-field answer.
No broad cohort is registered today: the 2020 keyword
export was retired 2026-11-06 (see note at the foot).
exact:  false marks a keyword cohort. Only exact cohorts count toward coverage,
because a keyword cohort is not the paper's own field.
ONE COHORT PER FIELD. A second exact cohort for the same field with overlapping
years puts the same works in two denominators, so a new export REPLACES the old
entry rather than joining it. tools/build-field-comparison.js warns when two
exact cohorts for one field overlap in years.
FWCI: the export tool can add a trailing FWCI column. When present the tool also
ranks each paper's FWCI against the cohort's own same-year FWCI distribution,
which is normalised for age and field at once. Five-column files still work.
Adding a Tier 1 or Tier 2 export from OpenAlex/README.md means adding one entry
here and re-running tools/build-field-comparison.js. No code change is needed.
reported_works is the count OQL returned at export time, kept so a change in
OpenAlex's data is visible rather than silent.
RETIRED 2026-11-06: the 'glyco-keyword-2020' cohort (works-2026-11-05T15-49-23.csv,
24,585 works, no FWCI column) was removed and its CSV deleted. It fed no percentile
and no coverage figure -- only exact cohorts do that -- so its loss moves no number
on the page. It was also the cohort on which the pandemic question looked large
(measured before deletion: 3.6% of rows holding 13.5% of citations, pulling p99 from
103 to 92). The pandemic exclusion itself was retired the same day at the user's
instruction: inside the two exact cohorts those rows are 0.5% and 0.3% of rows,
carrying 1% and 0.3% of citations, so no percentile on this page is computed on a
filtered cohort and the toggle that once offered one has been removed. To bring a
broad cohort back, export 'get articles since 2008 with (glycan OR glycosylation)
in the title or abstract, most cited first' with an FWCI
column and add an entry here.

cohorts.label: Glycosylation and Glycoproteins Research (primary topic), articles 2008+
cohorts.oql: get articles since 2008 in the topic [Glycosylation and Glycoproteins Research](T10602), most cited first
cohorts.note: Exact-field cohort for the glycoscience programme. Replaces the 2020-only export, which could not rank the 2011-2019 part of the record. Verified 25,326 parsed records against the API's own count, 2008-2026 with no missing year and 1,035-1,584 articles in every year, so same-year matching is well-populated throughout.

cohorts.label: Blood Coagulation and Thrombosis Mechanisms (primary topic), articles 2008+
cohorts.oql: get articles since 2008 in the topic [Blood Coagulation and Thrombosis Mechanisms](T10881), most cited first
cohorts.note: Exact-field cohort for the anticoagulation programme, at the user's instruction that anticoagulant work ranks against anticoagulant-like fields rather than glycoscience. Every anticoagulation paper in the record is dated before 2020, so a cohort beginning in 2020 would have ranked none of them. Verified 26,517 parsed records against the API's own count, 2008-2026 with no missing year.
